title: Horror — Beginner
summary: A single-player horror loop: perception with sight and audio, use, a stalk on a patrol timer, a creaking door, local health, and a save that keeps Alert and IsOpen together.

sections.title: Sight and sound
sections.why: Sense runs five times a second. A wall blocks the trace. A loud sound uses the same event.
reading: A horror hunter does not tick. Begin Play starts a timer, and the excerpt calls Graph_Sense every 0.2 seconds, looping. Sense line-traces. If the trace hits, the excerpt assigns Alert = 1.f. A wall on the visibility channel blocks the trace, so the hunter does not see through doors it has not opened. A loud sound, a dropped bottle or a sprint on a hard floor, calls the same Sense event. The hunter does not grow a second brain for audio.

UE5 perception components can replace this timer later. The sample keeps the rule visible: one event, a trace for line of sight, a float for how sure the hunter is. Alert at 1 is the sample's confirmed sight. A real stalk adds to Alert and lets it fall when the trace misses. The miss path in the sample does nothing, so a confirmed sight stays forever until you add the decay. That decay is a subtract on the miss, not a tick.

The player's interact trace is a different trace, from the camera, when the player uses something. It must not write Alert, or looking at the hunter would announce the player. The door timeline can play a creak, and that creak is an audio cue into Sense. Health does not sense. Save stores Alert so a load does not forget that the hunter was already sure.

Tracing every frame so the hunter never loses a peek is the expensive version, and it sees flicks the design wanted to forgive. 0.2 seconds is a glimpse. The audio cue is instant because the sound event calls Sense directly, not because the timer got faster.

The hunter's Sense trace is the other graph. Mixing them makes the player announce Alert every time they look at a door, and makes the hunter try to turn valves.

The excerpt is Graph_IA_Interact: a visibility trace, then ProcessEvent on Interact if bHit, else a log that nothing can be used. The else is the dark miss. It does not raise Alert. The door's own timeline moves the mesh after Interact tells it to. This graph does not play the timeline, or every usable actor would need a door curve.

sections.title: Stalking the route
sections.why: AdvancePatrol walks the route on a timer. Alert from Sense decides when the stalk leaves the route.
reading: The stalk is a patrol that can abandon the route. Begin Play sets a timer for AdvancePatrol at 1 second in the excerpt. The event flips direction and the A path assigns GoingRight = true. The B path is empty in the sample, so the walk back is unfinished. Alert, written by Sense, is what pulls the hunter off the route. This graph does not trace. If it traces, the hunter has two eyes and they will disagree.

Tick that steps the hunter also steps it during a pause menu and pays for a path the timer already chose. The route points are data. AdvancePatrol only picks the next one. When Alert is 1, a different event starts the chase. That event is not Tick either. It is a branch you add beside this timer, reading Alert.

The player's interact graph does not move the hunter. The door's IsOpen can block a route point. The hunter asks the door. It does not play the door timeline itself. Health on the hunter, if the player can fight, is a separate float from the player's health in the next lesson.
Save stores GoingRight and Alert together. Loading one without the other resumes a calm patrol while the hunter was already sure, or a chase with no direction.

sections.title: The creaking door
sections.why: Overlap plays a timeline. FlipFlop toggles IsOpen. The creak is the audio cue.
reading: A horror door moves on a timeline, not on Tick. Overlap, or the Interact call from the player, plays the timeline from the start. The excerpt builds a UTimelineComponent, adds a curve with keys at 0 and 1, binds update and finished, and calls PlayFromStart. FlipFlop remembers the direction. The A path sets IsOpen true. The B path sets it false. The creak is a sound played with the timeline, and that sound calls Sense so the hunter can hear the door.

Tick that yaws the mesh every frame also yaws it while the player is holding it still, and it never knows when it has arrived. The curve knows. IsOpen is the replicated fact if another player must see the door. The mesh is local, driven by the curve. Replicating the mesh transform every frame is the expensive version of a bool.

The hunter's patrol can read IsOpen before it picks a point. It does not play this timeline. The player's use graph only calls Interact. Perception does not open doors. Save stores IsOpen so a loaded game does not shut a door the player left open, which would also replay the creak and wake the hunter for free.
Filter the overlap so the hunter and the player do not both toggle the door in one step. The other actor has to be the one the design named.

sections.title: Single-player health
sections.why: This lesson is local health: subtract, clamp, and branch on zero. It is not the replicated graph.
reading: This horror lesson is single player, so health is local. The excerpt's Any Damage function assigns Health = FMath::Clamp((Health - Damage), 0.f, MaxHealth) and then branches if (Health == 0.f) to log Died. There is no HasAuthority and no OnRep, because there is no other machine. Do not paste the replicated graph here and do not leave the clamp off. A hit for more than the bar would otherwise store a negative number, and the death check for exactly zero would never pass.

The hunter calls this event when an attack lands. It does not subtract inside Sense or inside AdvancePatrol. Those graphs own Alert and direction. The door does not damage the player by opening. A trap that overlaps can call Any Damage. Tick damage, so the player bleeds while reading a note, happens with no attack.

The death log stands in for the fail function. Put the fail on the true pin, after the clamp, so a hit that does not reach zero does not restart the level. Save stores Health after the write. Loading a negative value means the clamp was skipped before the pack.
If the mode later adds a co-op partner, this is the lesson you replace with the replicated graph. Until then the local clamp is the whole rule.

sections.title: Save the house
sections.why: Begin Play restores Alert, Health, and IsOpen together.
reading: The horror slot packs Alert, Health, IsOpen, and GoingRight. Leave one out and the load lies: a shut door with the hunter already sure, or an open door that replays its creak into a calm house. Begin Play loads. The excerpt assigns SlotValue = 1.f and LoadSlot logs Loaded after a break stand-in. The real struct replaces that stand-in. The fields are the ones the other graphs write.

Tick that saves on every frame stores a door halfway through its curve and an Alert that Sense has not finished decaying. The creak plays again on load because IsOpen flips. Write the struct when the timeline finishes, or when the player passes a save point, not while the curve is playing.

Input assets and the hunter's mesh are not packed. The route points are project data. The next point index, or GoingRight, is enough to resume the stalk. Health must be the clamped value. A packed negative fails the death check later in a way the player cannot see coming.

Load order: apply IsOpen without replaying the creak, then apply Alert, then start the Sense timer and the patrol timer. Starting Sense first lets it trace before the doors are in the saved pose, and the hunter learns a lie.

Save the house closes on Save / load slot. Begin Play restores Alert, Health, and IsOpen together. Line 14 is `FHitResult Broken_tpl_saveload_break = FHitResult(); // node:tpl_save-load_break`. Begin Play stays on its own event and is not written from Save the house. IsOpen is packed and applied without playing the creak. Alert and Health are in the same struct. The assignment names the repair to keep.
